source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential facility is in one of the company national markets confirmed on its own homepage covering Oregon (Portland/Hillsboro), Texas (Dallas, Plano, Richardson), Ohio (West Chester, Cincinnati market), Kentucky (Louisville), Pennsylvania (Allentown, Collegeville, Philadelphia market), Virginia (Richmond), Minnesota (Chaska, Minneapolis market), and Arizona (Phoenix). Flexential was formed from the 2017 merger of ViaWest, founded 1999, and Peak 10, founded 2000, followed by a 2018 rebrand to Flexential. The company reports 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets, 3 million plus square feet of facilities, an 800 million dollar expansion investment, and a planned new campus on 110 acres in Kaufman County near Dallas. This specific state cluster was confirmed as an active Flexential market on the company own site, but no market specific founding, acquisition, or building history distinct from the general ViaWest and Peak 10 company story was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Flexential Louisville - Downtown in Louisville, Kentucky, publishes 3.09 MW of IT capacity across 61,080 square feet of technical space, operated by Flexential.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 309 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 77 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Flexential Louisville - Downtown holds 6 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), ISO 27001 (a certified information security management system), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA), SSAE 18 (the attestation standard underlying SOC reports). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Kentucky has 3 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 3 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 9.55 MW. Flexential Louisville - Downtown contributes 3.09 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
